verdict.tagline: Massive dinosaur survival buried under severe technical friction.
for_you_if: you want deep dinosaur taming and breeding mechanics
you can endure heavy resource grinding and survival loops
you enjoy expansive open worlds with extensive building options
not_for_you_if: you need stable launch performance and reliable connection tools
you lack massive hard drive space for the install
you want to avoid losing progress to save bugs

I got this game recommended and I gotta say: What is wrong with the performance of this game? Like, I'm no game dev, not at all, but how do you manage to make the game run so poorly 

I mean, my PC is definitely NOT the best but I can play all Resident Evil remakes at medium graphics 60 fps no problem, as well as GTA V Enhanced on High and other titles (+ it's over the system requirements), yet this game in LOW (and I mean FULL LOW RES mode) makes my PC struggle to maintain 60 fps... at 100% GPU usage! 💀💀

The main menu in itself constantly freezes for a whooping 30+ seconds and I figured that launching the game without Battleye AntiCheat GREATLY improves performance (as expected tho...) but to no avail, because the loading times are atrocious.

I have an SSD and even so, looking up on Reddit, I see a guy who says it's normal for the game to take 30~40 minutes to load you into the world on a HDD. My man must be the biggest fan of this game because HOW are you willing to wait that long to play 😭😭😭 other people mention SSD taking 5+ minutes at best, so I waited and waited

And guys, I'm not exaggerating when I say that at least 30 mins of playtime I have with this game is me looking at the loading screen. No cap, fr, I genuinely don't know how this game has so many positive reviews. Do everyone just have a streamer level GPU and a lightspeed SSD?

You can be sure I'm going to slap my friend for recommending me this game because the other 4 minutes of playtime I have is just me figuring out that the inventory opens with V... I have a question: [b]Why...?[/b] and why does pressing Tab opens a console? And "I" makes a funny noise 🤡

PS: This is why I support Demos so much! We need more Demos!!

Rating: 4/10 — Great Concept, Horrible Execution

ARK: Survival Evolved has one of the best concepts in the entire survival genre. The idea of waking up naked on a mysterious island, taming massive dinosaurs, building bases, and progressing from primitive tools to sci-fi technology is brilliant on paper.

Unfortunately, the actual execution is a complete mess. The biggest issue with this game is its utterly atrocious optimization. Even on high-end hardware, the performance is a joke—expect constant FPS drops, stutters, and freezes. The game is notoriously bloated, taking up an absurd amount of storage space for no justifiable reason.

Beyond the technical disasters, the gameplay is ruined by endless, disrespectful grinding, a clunky user interface, and countless game-breaking bugs that have been ignored for years. Unless you are playing on highly boosted private servers or with a group of friends who are willing to overlook a broken product, the official experience is just a frustrating, unpolished chore.
How does a game released in 2017 perform this bad I’m not even mad I’m just bewildered how they managed to make a game run so terribly (I know I’m on steam deck but still)

claims.claim: Loading into the game takes an extremely long time.

citations.review_text:
I got this game recommended and I gotta say: What is wrong with the performance of this game? Like, I'm no game dev, not at all, but how do you manage to make the game run so poorly 

I mean, my PC is definitely NOT the best but I can play all Resident Evil remakes at medium graphics 60 fps no problem, as well as GTA V Enhanced on High and other titles (+ it's over the system requirements), yet this game in LOW (and I mean FULL LOW RES mode) makes my PC struggle to maintain 60 fps... at 100% GPU usage! 💀💀

The main menu in itself constantly freezes for a whooping 30+ seconds and I figured that launching the game without Battleye AntiCheat GREATLY improves performance (as expected tho...) but to no avail, because the loading times are atrocious.

I have an SSD and even so, looking up on Reddit, I see a guy who says it's normal for the game to take 30~40 minutes to load you into the world on a HDD. My man must be the biggest fan of this game because HOW are you willing to wait that long to play 😭😭😭 other people mention SSD taking 5+ minutes at best, so I waited and waited

And guys, I'm not exaggerating when I say that at least 30 mins of playtime I have with this game is me looking at the loading screen. No cap, fr, I genuinely don't know how this game has so many positive reviews. Do everyone just have a streamer level GPU and a lightspeed SSD?

You can be sure I'm going to slap my friend for recommending me this game because the other 4 minutes of playtime I have is just me figuring out that the inventory opens with V... I have a question: [b]Why...?[/b] and why does pressing Tab opens a console? And "I" makes a funny noise 🤡

The game is playable. It runs 58-60fps on SteamDeck on mid-low setting, and runs 30-35fps on high-epic setting. The issue is even with the mid-low setting, the battery drainage is like an IPhone on life support. The loading time when I click to play single player take like 10-15 mins. It is pretty damm long.
As for story, I don't know, I'm new to this title. It's a survival game, I honestly don't expect much from the story.
As for theme, adventure always tag along with beauty, horror, and surprise elements. This game got all of that.
As for game mechanics, it is confusing and too complex sometimes. I feel like if I quit the game for like 2 or 3 years, the moment I come back I'll be a caveman.
Overall, the game is fine. Graphic is ok,  gameplay is fine, quite confusing at some point thou. The issue with this game is loading time is insanely long.

I wasn't around during the earliest days back when there were full servers, so i cant say how good it was back then (though some early community videos made it look pretty alive and hella fun. But as a new player trying it out for the first time, I had some issues immediately. Upon trying to simply start as single player game to get a feeling of the game i would have constant freezes in the main menu. I couldn't even change key binds, or even some video settings before it would happen. Only thing hat worked for me was suing a launch option to cap my fps. It worked only for one session for me unfortunately. I didn't get much of an experience because of said instability issues, but when the game was working, I did somewhat enjoy it. It's a shame because the idea of a survival game with dinosaurs a vast range of technology being at play was a very interesting idea for a game, but its plagued by many severe bugs, crashes, etc. Doesn't help that this game was abandoned by the developers for it's replacement "ARK Survival Ascended" (which is the same game in everyway including the bugs, albeit it is a graphic overhaul with some QoL features supposedly)

I also found information (while searching for technical fixes and general guides for the game) regarding some alleged shady practices from the publisher on not only how they treated the game itself but the community as well. (such as banning an account of a content creator for making a critical video on the state of the game. backing a large tribe who allegedly also was hardcore cheating by giving them blueprints or other in game advantages, general corporate greed, etc)

Given the issues presented, I don't exactly have a positive outlook on the ARK franchise, but i feel a lot of empathy for its community, they seem every passionate about the game and just want it to be better.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the early gameplay as a heavy grind involving cutting trees and mining rocks.

citations.review_text: Very dull, spent 5 hours cutting trees and mining rocks and nothing happened

12hrs already on a nonstop grind its fun like really fun but mods are game changers.

I would recommend primal fear and mods that make the game easier like dino storage V2 Creature finder Deluxe and Awesome SpyGlass and what not.

ARK is equal parts survival game and dinosaur chaos simulator. One minute you’re peacefully gathering berries, the next you’re getting chased across the beach by something ten times your size. Taming creatures and building massive bases is incredibly satisfying, especially with friends, though the game can be janky and brutally grindy at times. Still, few games match the feeling of riding your own T-Rex into battle.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe dinosaur pathfinding as problematic, noting that following creatures struggle with gates and path themselves off cliffs.

citations.review_text: This game is the single worst game I have every played. My hate for this game spills out of every pore in my body the instant I see it in my library. This stupid game takes up over 150 GB and runs like its in early access. Everything in this game makes me angry. The impossible to hit enemies, the horrible tame AI failing to do the simplest task, the lack of guidance to tame any dinosaur, even the inventory is jank. The only SPECK of joy I felt was the character creation, but even that loses its whimsy after a good 2 minutes. During the day the glare is so bad it flashbangs you (and to my knowledge there is no glare setting), and at night it is so dark even with a torch you still can't see. Base lighting is impossible, there has not been a good looking building in ARK history, and the signs and graves are near impossible to read. This game takes like 20 minutes to load any world and looks horrible on any setting.

The glitches in this game are unbearable. Stuck inside a dino, dino stuck inside building, dino stuck in rock, about to tame a dino but you can't because you a stuck inside that dino. AI pathway of dinos following you is very bad, they won't follow you through gates, you tell them not to follow you, but they still do, they path themselves to you by falling off a cliff despite no cliff between you can dino, etc. 
It would be great if there was an option to save game before these game haulting glitches. Be able to have mutlible backup save files would help greatly, but it this game dosn't allow you to. It just saves when you quit. There are game walkthoughs about how to unglitch your dinos. These videos shouldn't even need to exist. This game eats most of your hard drive for this epic mess. 
I am going to try to keep playing. But this game is harder to play than anything Bethesda has made.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that saved game data can be lost due to bugs, crashes, or characters randomly being deleted.

citations.review_text: This game is a pittiful pit of despair and agony, onlly comparable to the last circles of hell. A buggy, addictive mess that keeps pulling me back in everytime I'm about to forget it. I had it on epic games, uninstalled it there but somehow it crossed my mind to purchase it on steam, I cannot escape this game, no matter how many times I uninstall it, change my gaming console to a PC and back or switch to another gaming platform. [h2]Nota Geral | Overall Rating[/h2]
⭐⭐⭐⭐

[b]ARK: Survival Evolved é um daqueles jogos que te fazem sentir uma mistura de admiração e raiva quase na mesma proporção. A Studio Wildcard criou um dos survivals mais ambiciosos já feitos, com domesticação de dinossauros, construção de bases e um enredo de ficção científica surpreendentemente bom escondido por trás da fórmula de sobrevivência. O problema é que o jogo insiste em te punir de um jeito cruel demais: o grind é absurdo, e perder horas de progresso porque um predador apareceu do nada enquanto você domava um dinossauro é o tipo de frustração que só não afunda a nota geral porque o resto da experiência é bom o suficiente pra compensar.[/b]

[i]ARK: Survival Evolved is one of those games that makes you feel a mix of admiration and rage in almost equal measure. Studio Wildcard created one of the most ambitious survival games ever made, with dinosaur taming, base building, and a surprisingly good sci-fi plot hidden behind the survival formula. The problem is that the game insists on punishing you in a way that's too cruel: the grind is absurd, and losing hours of progress because a predator showed up out of nowhere while you were taming a dinosaur is the kind of frustration that only fails to sink the overall score because the rest of the experience is good enough to make up for it.[/i]

[h2]Jogabilidade | Gameplay[/h2]
⭐⭐⭐⭐

[b]A jogabilidade de domesticação e construção é genuinamente viciante quando funciona. Ver seu primeiro dinossauro domado depois de um processo longo e tenso é uma das sensações mais gratificantes que já senti num survival, e o sistema de construção de bases dá liberdade real pra criar estruturas complexas. O problema é justamente o desequilíbrio entre risco e recompensa: o jogo te faz investir horas domando uma criatura, e um único descuido, um predador aparecendo do nada ou um grupo emboscando você, pode apagar esse progresso inteiro em segundos. Não é difícil no bom sentido, é pun…

I bought ARK when it first launched and put 840 hours into it in a little over a year before finally walking away in September 2018.

Despite this being a negative review, I want to start by saying something positive.

ARK gave me some of my favorite gaming memories ever.

It was unlike anything else at the time. Survival, base building, taming dinosaurs, breeding, exploring massive maps—there was nothing quite like it. I joined a PvP server, but instead of constant griefing, it became a community. Most of us treated it like PvE with PvP enabled. We helped each other, welcomed new players, and built friendships instead of trying to wipe each other every night.

In fact, I met friends on that server that I'm still talking to almost 10 years later. That's something very few games can say.

We dealt with map changes that forced us to move our base multiple times. It was frustrating, but we understood the game was evolving. Eventually we built what we thought would be our forever base.

Then Wildcard introduced cross-server transfers.

That single update destroyed our server.

Alpha Tribes from other servers could suddenly transfer in with years of progress, powerful dinosaurs, and far more time invested than the average player. They weren't interested in joining our community—they came to wipe it.

Bases disappeared.

Breeding lines disappeared.

Entire tribes quit.

Our little community that had been thriving for years was gone within weeks.

That was the end of ARK for me.

Fast forward to 2023.

Wildcard announced ARK: Survival Ascended, rebuilt in Unreal Engine 5.

Instead of upgrading existing owners like many studios have done with engine upgrades, they expected everyone to buy the game again. Originally they even planned to bundle it with ARK 2 before community backlash changed those plans.

The part that still bothers me in 2026 is this:

ARK 2 still doesn't exist.

Official ARK: Survival Evolved servers were shut down, eve…

Even in 2026, ARK: Survival Evolved is still one of the craziest survival games ever made. With all DLCs installed, the game feels massive — every map has its own atmosphere, creatures, challenges, and story. From surviving on The Island to exploring Aberration, Extinction, Genesis, and Fjordur, the amount of content is honestly insane.

The dinosaur taming system is still unmatched. Building giant bases, breeding powerful creatures, exploring caves, fighting bosses, and surviving with friends creates moments no other game really delivers. The graphics may show their age sometimes, and the game can still be buggy, but ARK’s scale and freedom make up for it.

What makes ARK special is that every playthrough becomes its own story. One day you’re getting destroyed by a raptor, the next day you’re flying across the map on a mutated wyvern army. Few games give that feeling of progression.

With all extras and DLCs, this is easily hundreds or even thousands of hours of gameplay. If you enjoy survival, dinosaurs, open-world exploration, and co-op chaos, ARK is still worth playing in 2026.

Form me, it worth all cents i have paid for this game in all DLC.

claims.claim: The game features taming and breeding mechanics for dinosaurs.

citations.review_text:
The Only Game Where You Can Get Bullied By A Dodo
I bought this game thinking it would be a majestic, prehistoric adventure where I’d tame a majestic Tyrannosaurus Rex and ride it into the sunset. Instead, my first six hours consisted of spawning completely naked on a beach, punching a palm tree until my hands bled, and instantly getting liquidated by a dinosaur the size of a chicken that spat blinding venom directly into my eyes. ARK isn't just a survival game; it’s an ecosystem designed to remind you that you are at the absolute bottom of the food chain.

The Wake-Up Call (Hour 1 to 50)
The early game experience is pure, unmitigated comedy. You will spend forty-five minutes carefully gathering fiber, thatch, and stones to build a humble 2x2 wooden shack to call home. You'll step inside, feel a profound sense of accomplishment, and look out the window just in time to see a wild Spinosaurus wander down from the mountains. Within three seconds, your house, your bed, your storage boxes, and your physical form will be utterly erased from existence. You don't own property in ARK; you are merely renting it from the local wildlife until they decide they want a snack.

The Absolute Absurdity of Taming
The taming mechanic in this game is wild if you think about it from an outside perspective. To make a dinosaur your best friend, you have to beat it unconscious with a club, shove a hundred berries or raw meat down its throat while it’s asleep, and sit next to it for three actual, real-life hours protecting it from getting bitten by a passing raptor. If you leave for five minutes to get a glass of water, a random bug will bite your future pet, ruining its taming effectiveness, and you'll have to start the whole existential crisis over again. But the moment you finally put a saddle on a Triceratops, you forget all the trauma.

Alpha Tribes and the PvP Nightmare

10/10. Would sacrifice my sleep schedule for baby dinosaurs again.

Studio Wildcard created one of the most ambitious survival games ever made, with dinosaur taming, base building, and a surprisingly good sci-fi plot hidden behind the survival formula. The problem is that the game insists on punishing you in a way that's too cruel: the grind is absurd, and losing hours of progress because a predator showed up out of nowhere while you were taming a dinosaur is the kind of frustration that only fails to sink the overall score because the rest of the experience is good enough to make up for it.[/i]

O problema é justamente o desequilíbrio entre risco e recompensa: o jogo te faz investir horas domando uma criatura, e um único descuido, um predador aparecendo do nada ou um grupo emboscando você, pode apagar esse progresso inteiro em segundos. The Only Game Where You Can Get Bullied By A Dodo
I bought this game thinking it would be a majestic, prehistoric adventure where I’d tame a majestic Tyrannosaurus Rex and ride it into the sunset. Instead, my first six hours consisted of spawning completely naked on a beach, punching a palm tree until my hands bled, and instantly getting liquidated by a dinosaur the size of a chicken that spat blinding venom directly into my eyes. ARK isn't just a survival game; it’s an ecosystem designed to remind you that you are at the absolute bottom of the food chain.

The Wake-Up Call (Hour 1 to 50)
The early game experience is pure, unmitigated comedy. You will spend forty-five minutes carefully gathering fiber, thatch, and stones to build a humble 2x2 wooden shack to call home. You'll step inside, feel a profound sense of accomplishment, and look out the window just in time to see a wild Spinosaurus wander down from the mountains. Within three seconds, your house, your bed, your storage boxes, and your physical form will be utterly erased from existence. You don't own property in ARK; you are merely renting it from the local wildlife until they decide they want a snack.

The Absolute Absurdity of Taming
The taming mechanic in this game is wild if you think about it from an outside perspective. To make a dinosaur your best friend, you have to beat it unconscious with a club, shove a hundred berries or raw meat down its throat while it’s asleep, and sit next to it for three actual, real-life hours protecting it from getting bitten by a passing raptor. If you leave for five minutes to get a glass of water, a random bug will bite your future pet, ruining its taming effectiveness, and you'll have to start the whole existential crisis over again. But the moment you finally put a saddle on a Triceratops, you forget all the trauma.
